title: [B1 • Band 5.0] Bài 212: Cracking the Code: The Decipherment of Linear B
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 212 (LEVEL B1 • BAND 5.0)

Cracking the Code: The Decipherment of Linear B

Paragraph 1. In the spring of 1900, British archaeologist Sir Arthur Evans began digging at Knossos on the island of Crete. Within days, he uncovered the grand ruins of a Bronze Age palace, along with thousands of baked clay tablets carrying two unknown writing systems. Evans called the older picture-like script Linear A and the younger, sharper script Linear B. Convinced he had found a separate island culture, Evans firmly insisted that Linear B had zero connection to classical Greek.

Paragraph 2. For over forty years, scholars could not read a single line of Linear B. Because the clay tablets were meant only as short-term office notes, they survived only when palace fires accidentally baked the soft clay into hard ceramic. Progress stalled further because experts had no two-language stone like Egypt's Rosetta Stone to match unknown signs with readable words. Evans passed away in 1941 without ever solving the puzzle.

Paragraph 3. The real conceptual breakthrough came from a patient American teacher named Alice Kober at Brooklyn College in the 1940s. Short on wartime supplies, Kober cut thousands of index cards from used exam papers to track symbol patterns. She noticed groups of signs sharing the same starting symbols but ending differently, showing grammatical endings similar to Latin. Before her early death in 1950, Kober built a mathematical grid proving each Linear B sign stood for a consonant paired with a vowel.

Paragraph 4. Young British architect Michael Ventris took up Kober's grid. At first, Ventris agreed with Evans that Linear B was not Greek. However, when he tested sound values on known Cretan places like Knossos and Amnisos, familiar Greek words suddenly appeared. On 1 July 1952, Ventris announced on BBC radio that Linear B was an ancient form of Greek written five hundred years before the poet Homer.

Paragraph 5. Working alongside Cambridge scholar John Chadwick, Ventris confirmed that Linear B recorded Mycenaean Greek. Rather than heroic stories, the tablets held detailed tax accounts listing quantities of barley, olive oil, sheep, and bronze weapons. They also named Greek gods like Zeus and Athena, pushing verified Greek language history back by more than half a millennium.

q6.text: Why did scholars struggle to read Linear B for over forty years?
options: A. All the clay tablets broke into dust after excavation.
B. The palace ruins were closed to researchers until 1950.
C. Linear B contained more than ten thousand different pictures.
D. Experts lacked a two-language key like the Rosetta Stone.

steps: Đoạn 2: Không có phiến đá song ngữ như Rosetta Stone để đối chiếu.

q7.text: What important pattern did Alice Kober notice in Linear B symbols?
options: A. Every tablet started with the name of King Minos.
B. Word endings changed to show grammar, similar to Latin.
C. Symbols were written backwards from right to left.
D. Linear B used exact copies of Egyptian hieroglyphs.

steps: Đoạn 3: Các từ có phần đầu giống nhau nhưng phần đuôi biến đổi theo ngữ pháp giống tiếng Latin.

q8.text: How did Michael Ventris realize Linear B sounded like Greek?
options: A. By applying sound values to local place names in Crete
B. By discovering a Greek dictionary inside Knossos palace
C. By comparing Homer's poems with old Etruscan books
D. By asking local farmers on Crete to read the clay signs

steps: Đoạn 4: Thử ghép giá trị âm vào tên các địa danh ở đảo Crete như Knossos và Amnisos.

q9.text: Who worked with Michael Ventris to confirm Linear B was Mycenaean Greek?
options: A. Sir Arthur Evans
B. Alice Kober
C. John Chadwick
D. King Minos

q10.text: What major historical change did solving Linear B cause?
options: A. It proved King Minos built the pyramids in Egypt.
B. It pushed verified Greek language history back by over 500 years.
C. It showed that ancient Greeks never kept written tax records.
D. It revealed that Homer wrote his poems in Linear A.

steps: Đoạn 5: Đẩy lùi lịch sử chữ viết tiếng Hy Lạp được xác thực sớm hơn 500 năm.
